lines.en: Excuse me, **could you tell me how to get to** the Central Library?
lines.pt: Com licença, você poderia me dizer como chegar à Biblioteca Central?

lines.en: Sure! **Go straight** on this street for two blocks.
lines.pt: Claro! Siga reto por esta rua por dois quarteirões.

lines.en: Then **turn left at the** bank. You’ll see a big fountain on your right.
lines.pt: Depois vire à esquerda no banco. Você vai ver uma grande fonte à sua direita.

lines.en: Is it far? Should I take a bus?
lines.pt: É longe? Devo pegar um ônibus?

lines.en: No, it’s a five-minute walk. **Walk past** the fountain and it’s on the corner, across from the post office.
lines.pt: Não, é uma caminhada de cinco minutos. Passe pela fonte e fica na esquina, em frente ao correio.

lines.en: Straight two blocks, left at the bank, past the fountain. Got it.
lines.pt: Reto dois quarteirões, esquerda no banco, passando a fonte. Entendi.

lines.en: Perfect. **You can’t miss it** — it has tall stone columns.
lines.pt: Perfeito. Você não tem como errar: tem colunas altas de pedra.

lines.en: Thanks so much! You’ve been really helpful.
lines.pt: Muito obrigado! Você foi muito prestativa.

pages.title: Detailed directions

situation.text: You are in a city you do not know. You ask a stranger how to get to a place and check that you understood each step.

pages.goal: By the end of the class you can ask for directions, follow several steps using landmarks and confirm what you understood.
canDo: Ask: Could you tell me how to get to…?
Understand Go straight / Turn left at…
Use landmarks: past, across from, on the corner
Repeat the steps to check: Got it?
pages.think: When someone gives you directions in Portuguese, do you use street names, distances or landmarks? Which one helps you most?

Mostre os 4 critérios.
group: Cada estudante cita um lugar perto da escola/casa.
Anote no quadro como landmarks.
extra: Do you use maps on your phone?
Have you ever been lost in a new city?
support: Aceite palavras soltas e reformule em frases.

pages.title: Cultural snapshot — Landmarks
pages.intro: People explain routes in different ways around the world. Look and guess before you read.

cards.note: In many U.S. cities with grid streets, people say “two blocks” and “turn left at the corner”.
Simple directions work in almost every situation: go straight, turn left, turn right.
“Turn left at the bank” is easier to follow than a street name you cannot see.

qs.q: Why are landmarks useful in directions?
qs.pt: Por que pontos de referência ajudam?

levels.A2: They are easy to see and remember.
levels.B1: A visible bank or fountain is easier to find than a street name.
levels.B2: Landmarks give visual confirmation that you are on the right route, especially for visitors.

qs.q: What does “You can’t miss it” mean?
qs.pt: O que significa “You can’t miss it”?

levels.A2: It is easy to see, so you will find it.
levels.B1: The place is very noticeable, so you should not have trouble finding it.
levels.B2: It reassures the listener that the place is obvious, though it is not a guarantee.

qs.q: How can you check that you understood?

levels.B1: Summarize the route and ask “Is that right?”
levels.B2: Paraphrase the main steps and ask for confirmation of the one you are least sure about.

pages.compare: In Brazil, directions often use landmarks too (“depois da padaria, vira à esquerda”) and “é logo ali”. In English, “just around the corner” and “a five-minute walk” are the equivalent. What do you say?

teach.goal: Mostrar como as direções são dadas: blocos, esquerda/direita e pontos de referência.
solo: Mostre os 3 cartões e peça hipóteses.

answers: Q1: easy to see and remember.
extra: Do you prefer maps or spoken directions?
What is the most famous landmark near you?
stretch: B2: explique por que repetir ajuda a evitar erros.

Mostre o texto no final.

extra: Is the library on the left or right?

support: Use “Slow” e pause após cada passo.

patterns.name: Giving directions (imperative)

patterns.name: Describing position
patterns.formula: **It’s** + on the corner / across from / next to + place

ex: Could you tell me how to get to the library?

pages.title: Pronunciation lab — natural American English
pages.tip: In directions the stressed words are the ones that carry the route: “Turn LEFT at the BANK”. Small words are weak and quick.

own.prompt: Write a three-step direction from your home to a nearby place.
own.criteria: Say it twice: slowly, then with strong key words. Could your partner follow the route?

group: Coro, depois duplas.
Cada estudante dá uma direção.
answers: Identify 1: left at the bank · Identify 2: two blocks

errors.w: Pronunciar todas as palavras com a mesma força
“left” e “right” confundidos por falta de ênfase

support: Reduza a velocidade e conte as batidas.

pages.goal: Each group must give clear directions with landmarks and check that the listener understood.

pages.title: Writing — a small real-life task
pages.task: Write a message to a friend explaining how to get from the station to your home or favorite café.
pages.model: Hi Raj! From the station, go straight for two blocks, then turn left at the bank. Walk past the fountain and the café is on the corner, across from the post office. You can’t miss it! See you soon.
checklist: I used at least three steps.
I used Go straight / Turn left / Walk past.
I closed with “You can’t miss it” or similar.
pages.tip: Fix only 2–3 priority points and show a more natural way to say the same idea.

teach.goal: Produção escrita curta: dar direções por escrito.
solo: Corrija 2–3 pontos prioritários.
group: Troquem os textos; o colega desenha a rota.

criteria.name: Language use

criteria.name: Pronunciation

criteria.name: Interaction
criteria.desc: Responde, pergunta, esclarece e desenvolve a conversa.

interpret.text: Needs more support. Revisit the main patterns with guided practice before the next lesson.
Functional performance. Work on the lowest criteria in the next lesson.
Good control. Add follow-up questions and longer answers.
Strong performance. Move to a more demanding situation.

pages.title: Level up — the same situation from A1 to C2
pages.intro: The situation stays the same; the language grows in length, nuance and autonomy.

ladder.goal: Ask for a place with a few words.

ladder.say: Could you tell me how to get to the library?
ladder.goal: Ask politely and follow simple steps.

ladder.say: Go straight for two blocks, then turn left at the bank; it’s across from the post office.
If you take the second street on the left, you’ll see the library right after the fountain.
You’re about ten minutes away on foot, though if the street is closed, it may be quicker to cut through the park.
It’s not the most obvious route, but if you trust the river, you’ll find it tucked behind the old columns.

pages.note: This progression is illustrative: complex sentences do not define a level on their own. CEFR also considers comprehension, autonomy, fluency, accuracy, interaction and appropriateness.

teach.goal: Mostrar a progressão sem criar seis metodologias.
